re_line: Russian jets trigger KADIZ alert · Nvidia/Huang KOSPI rebound · Kim Yo Jong threatens Swiss office · Lee cabinet reshuffle analysis · DOJ seeks $1.1B DPRK crypto forfeiture
morning_memo: About five Russian warplanes entered KADIZ, approached Ulleung Island, triggering an air raid alert later corrected and lifted.
KOSPI surged 6.32% to reclaim 5,006, its first close above 5,000 in three sessions, on Jensen Huang's Nvidia reinstatement.
Kim Yo Jong threatened to force closure of Switzerland's newly opened Pyongyang diplomatic office over sanctions on a children's camp.

key_stat.label: KOSPI single-session gain on Jensen Huang reinstatement
key_stat.context: The Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m., the first activation since November 10, as chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK hynix rallied on Huang's return as Nvidia CEO.

imagery_report.label: North Korea's two Choe Hyon-class destroyers tracked
imagery_report.headline: Satellite imagery places Kang Kon at Mayang Island naval base, Choe Hyon at Nampo; shipyard expansion visible at Chongjin and Nampo
imagery_report.body: Daily NK analysis of 2026 satellite imagery shows North Korea's two new 5,000-ton Choe Hyon-class destroyers have split between coasts: the Kang Kon is moored at the Mayang Island naval base and the Choe Hyon remains at Nampo. Shipyards in Chongjin and Nampo show expansion consistent with additional large-warship construction.

source_links.label: Daily NK, Satellite images track North Korea's two new destroyers

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after more than two years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12. Daily NK satellite imagery analyzed Nov 24 places the Kang Kon at Mayang Island naval base and the Choe Hyon at Nampo, with shipyard expansion visible at Chongjin and Nampo consistent with additional large-warship construction.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: NK News Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed through November 15, 2026 confirms trucks filling Sinuiju customs facility from October 16, the day after the New Yalu River Bridge officially opened, with activity peaking October 19–20. A wall of 40-foot containers bearing Maersk and COSCO markings was visible on the Chinese side. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reported November 18 that Sinuiju markets are overflowing with Chinese goods but a severe cash shortage means almost nobody is buying, with vendors describing a 'trading cliff.' Daily NK reported November 23 that low-income families in Sinuiju are sinking into crisis as market prices for food and daily necessities soar despite state promotion of Sinuiju development as a model for regional growth.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: Herald Economy reported November 23 that a North Korean vessel marked 'Marine Police' was spotted near Yeonpyeong Island, with the ROK Joint Chiefs confirming they are tracking and monitoring the vessel. As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20, 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14, 2026 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips. NK News reported November 24 that the Ukrainian military struck the cargo freighter Angara, one of the four vessels in the documented arms-transfer fleet, in a drone attack that also sank the Russian corvette Merkury.

rok_government.action: MND summons Russian military attaché over KADIZ intrusion, lodges formal protest
rok_government.detail: The defense ministry summoned Russian Embassy military attaché Nikolai Marchenko to lodge a formal complaint after about five Russian warplanes entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) early Tuesday, approaching Ulleung Island. The Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed no airspace violation occurred but said the aircraft 'approached right up to the edge of violating territorial airspace.'

rok_government.official: Overseas Safety Planning Officer Cho Joo-sung
rok_government.action: MOFA convenes emergency review of 15 Middle East missions amid Hormuz shipping attacks
rok_government.detail: Foreign Minister **Cho Hyun**'s ministry held a joint headquarters-mission situation review on November 24, chaired by Overseas Safety Planning Officer Cho Joo-sung, with 15 Middle East posts attending. The ministry cited ongoing fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and Houthi rebels, Iran's attack on a Bahrain civilian industrial facility, and successive tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz as prompting heightened alertness.

rok_government.action: Cabinet meeting approves Sejong relocation of 31 agencies; gender-equality office expansion deferred
rok_government.detail: The 50th Cabinet meeting, chaired by President **Lee Jae-myung** at Cheong Wa Dae, approved a plan to relocate 31 agencies employing 5,460 public servants to Sejong by 2031 at an estimated cost of approximately 1.65 trillion won. A draft expanding gender-equality policy offices in 13 agencies was deferred after several ministers requested that agency-specific characteristics and the office title be reconsidered.

rok_government.action: Education ministry activates dedicated AI cheating response team; announces RF detectors and body cameras for national exams
rok_government.detail: Following President Lee Jae-myung's order for a cross-government investigation, the Education Ministry activated a dedicated AI cheating response team and announced plans to introduce radio-frequency detectors, mobile CCTV, and supervisor body cameras for national qualification exams. Using a smart device during a school-administered exam will result in zero marks for all subjects that day and possible expulsion.

rok_government.action: FSC publishes draft Digital Asset Basic Act; caps exchange shareholding at 20%
rok_government.detail: The Financial Services Commission released the government's draft Digital Asset Basic Act, which caps any single shareholder's stake in a cryptocurrency exchange at 20 percent. FSC Chair Lee Eok-won separately warned that stablecoins risk circumventing capital-movement regulations and called for bank-centered issuance.

calendar_watch.headline: Seoul Metro general strike threatened from first trains
calendar_watch.detail: Three Seoul Metro labor unions plan an indefinite general strike from the first trains Wednesday after final talks on wages, 2,212 job cuts, and safety staffing ended without agreement on November 24.

calendar_watch.headline: Suneung scores released; Education Ministry decides penalties
calendar_watch.detail: South Korea's Education Ministry committee will announce penalties for all 111 alleged AI-cheating cases before scores are released on December 11, per government statements following the November 19 College Scholastic Ability Test.

rok_assembly.action: Confirmation hearing for Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-chul held; opposition demands answer on presidential charge dismissal
rok_assembly.detail: Justice minister nominee **Lee Yong-chul** declined to commit to directing prosecutors to drop charges against President Lee Jae-myung during his confirmation hearing, saying he would not 'excessively exercise' prosecutorial authority. The hearing covered a special counsel tasked with investigating whether prosecutors abused authority in bringing 12 cases against the president, including allegations from his 2010–2018 tenure as Seongnam mayor.

rok_assembly.detail: The budget subcommittee deferred review of the Blue House special activity fund budget after ruling and opposition parties clashed, with the Democratic Party seeking to maintain the original amount and the People Power Party calling for reductions.

top_stories.headline: Russian warplanes approach Ulleung Island, triggering air raid alert and fighter scramble
top_stories.body: About five Russian warplanes entered the KADIZ over the East Sea early Tuesday and approached Ulleung Island close enough that the Joint Chiefs of Staff pre-emptively issued an air raid alert and scrambled fighter jets; no airspace violation was confirmed. The interior ministry's emergency alert incorrectly stated an airspace violation, and North Gyeongsang Province's cancellation notice mistakenly described the aircraft as suspected North Korean planes. The defense ministry summoned Russian military attaché Nikolai Marchenko to lodge a formal protest; SBS reported this was the third KADIZ intrusion by Russian aircraft in November alone.

top_stories.headline: Kim Yo Jong threatens to force closure of Switzerland's newly opened Pyongyang mission over children's camp sanctions
top_stories.body: **Kim Yo Jong** issued a KCNA statement Tuesday saying she would urge North Korea to consider 'withdrawing' the Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang, opened only weeks earlier, after Bern sanctioned a North Korean children's camp that had hosted Russian students. She called Switzerland's move 'an open hostile act' and 'a serious infringement upon the sovereignty of the DPRK.' The threat follows Pyongyang's earlier warning to the United Kingdom over separate sanctions, suggesting a pattern of using newly opened diplomatic channels as leverage.

top_stories.headline: KOSPI surges 6.32% to reclaim 5,000 as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
top_stories.body: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index rose *297.49 points, or 6.32 percent*, to close at 5,006.03, reclaiming the 5,000-point mark for the first time in three sessions, as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix rallied on Nvidia's unanimous board reinstatement of **Jensen Huang** as president and CEO. Nvidia's board said it had consulted senior US government officials before concluding Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk; Huang had stepped down November 12 after reports of an extramarital relationship with a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia has pledged to supply 260,000 graphics processing units to South Korea and Samsung and SK hynix supply high-bandwidth memory for Nvidia's AI processors.
top_stories.src_line: Korea Herald / Korea Times / Yonhap English

top_stories.headline: US DOJ seeks civil forfeiture of $1.17B in cryptocurrency stolen by North Korean hackers from Binance
top_stories.body: The US Department of Justice filed a civil forfeiture complaint in the US District Court for the District of Columbia on Monday seeking to recover *$1.17 billion* in USD Coin frozen after North Korean cyber actors stole it from Binance; $823 million was held in a single virtual wallet address. The complaint targets funds frozen following an October theft attributed to DPRK-linked actors.

also_today.headline: Seoul's cabinet reshuffle signals Washington it was heard, but dialogue-first North Korea policy intact
also_today.body_text: NK News analysis by **Jeongmin Kim** finds the joint exit of Unification Minister Chung Dong-young and NIS Director Lee Jong-seok, leading figures of the so-called pro-autonomy camp, is the message to Washington, while nominee Hong Ihk-pyo's appointment as unification minister does not indicate Seoul is abandoning its engagement-first approach to Pyongyang.

also_today.headline: Seoul preparing humanitarian repatriation of North Koreans rescued from drifting fishing boat Nov 3
also_today.body_text: A Unification Ministry spokesperson confirmed Tuesday that repatriation procedures are underway for an unspecified number of North Koreans taken into ROK custody on November 3 after their fishing boat was found drifting in the East Sea; the ministry declined to disclose crew numbers.

also_today.headline: Korea and Brazil launch inaugural defense industry joint committee in Brasilia
also_today.body_text: The Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) and Brazil's Ministry of Defense held the first meeting of a joint defense industry committee in Brasilia on Monday, signing a letter of intent to strengthen cooperation and agreeing to explore government-to-government contracts and joint development projects. Korea Aerospace Industries, Hyundai Rotem, Hanwha Aerospace, and LIG D&A attended to present weapons systems.

business_economy.headline: KOSPI adds 6.32% to close at 5,006 on Jensen Huang reinstatement; buy-side sidecar activated
business_economy.body_text: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index recovered from a two-day rout, gaining 297.49 points to close at 5,006.03 as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix rallied. The Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m., suspending program-trading buy orders for five minutes, the first such activation since November 10.

business_economy.headline: South Korea weighing potential $3B international bond sale
business_economy.body_text: South Korea is considering a potential $3 billion international bond sale, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, as the government manages financing needs amid elevated interest rates.

business_economy.headline: Korea secures January crude oil at over 75% of prior-year level as Middle East tensions persist
business_economy.body_text: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said January crude oil procurement has reached more than 75 percent of the prior year's level, up from more than 50 percent the previous week. South Korea separately asked Qatar for priority liquefied natural gas supplies once Strait of Hormuz production and shipping normalize.

business_economy.headline: Hanwha Aerospace to build 180MW defense AI data center in Changwon
business_economy.body_text: Hanwha Aerospace announced plans to construct a 180-megawatt defense artificial intelligence data center in Changwon, targeting military AI applications.

northeast_asia.headline: Chinese ambassador hosts DPRK Vice Minister of External Economic Relations in Pyongyang, pledges closer cooperation
northeast_asia.body_text: Chinese Ambassador **Wang Yajun** hosted North Korean Vice Minister of External Economic Relations **Ryu Un Hae** at the Chinese Embassy in Pyongyang on Monday, pledging to implement the 'important consensus' reached by the two countries' leaders and develop practical cooperation in trade and other fields. The meeting occurred as trade and exchanges between the two countries continue to grow following the New Yalu River Bridge opening in October.

northeast_asia.headline: China extends US export controls suspension on gallium and germanium by two months ahead of Xi's US visit
northeast_asia.body_text: China's Ministry of Commerce extended by two months, until January 27, 2027, its suspension of tightened export controls on gallium, germanium, and other dual-use critical minerals to the United States, with the move timed ahead of President **Xi Jinping**'s planned visit to the US in December. The suspension affects critical mineral supply chains that South Korean chipmakers and battery manufacturers rely on.

gallup_spotlight.finding: 47% of respondents cited 'economic issues' as the top priority for the government ahead of next year, per a Gallup Korea poll reported November 22, 2026.

rok_personnel.name: Hong Ihk-pyo
rok_personnel.detail: President Lee Jae-myung nominated former progressive lawmaker Hong Ihk-pyo as the new unification minister as part of a cabinet reshuffle announced Monday that also nominated new nominees for the National Intelligence Service director and foreign ministry positions. NK News analysis describes the joint exit of Unification Minister Chung Dong-young and NIS Director Lee Jong-seok as the reshuffle's signal to Washington.

opeds_today.headline: (Brief 2026-30) Restructuring of North Korea's Foreign Policy and Changes in Relations with Major Powers
opeds_today.central_argument: Since the 2019 Hanoi breakdown, North Korea has systematically restructured its foreign policy around nuclear-armed state status, expanding strategic cooperation with China and Russia while redefining inter-Korean relations as relations between two hostile states rather than pursuing negotiated reunification.
opeds_today.summary: Choi argues that North Korea's foreign policy realignment cannot be explained through individual bilateral shifts but reflects a coherent doctrine anchored in the 'Our State First' principle and Kim Jong Un's assertion that nuclear capability confers a new national status. The brief covers North Korea's dismantling of unification-related institutions since late 2023 and its repositioning of relations with the United States as contingent on Washington accepting DPRK nuclear status. It connects this structural shift to Pyongyang's demand for a qualitatively different framework before any resumption of diplomacy.

opeds_today.headline: South Korea Cannot Police Its Way Out of AI Cheating
opeds_today.central_argument: South Korea's response to AI-assisted cheating, adding proctors, RF detectors, and criminal sanctions, treats symptoms rather than the structural problem of an examination system that rewards finding correct answers rather than reasoning in an AI-driven society.
opeds_today.summary: The piece documents the November 19 Suneung incident, the first exam to trigger a nationwide emergency alert to find hidden phones, in which 111 alleged cheating cases were detected, five involving smart devices. It recounts that the top scorer on the tax exam confessed to AI cheating and that existing proposals to move toward essay-based testing by 2033 and abolish the Suneung by 2040 face grading-fairness concerns. The article argues enforcement measures alone cannot resolve the deeper incompatibility between the exam's design and an AI-abundant environment.

opeds_today.headline: Can Seoul avoid being sidelined in Trump's great-power diplomacy?
opeds_today.central_argument: The first-ever US-China-Russia summit in Shenzhen, which produced a joint peace declaration silent on the Korean Peninsula, poses a concrete risk that South Korea's core security priorities, North Korea's nuclear program, wartime operational control transfer, and nuclear-powered submarines, will be traded away in great-power bargaining Seoul cannot directly influence.
opeds_today.summary: The analysis surveys South Korean expert concern following the Shenzhen summit that Seoul faces structural marginalization as Trump pursues parallel engagement with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. It notes the joint declaration made no explicit reference to the Korean Peninsula and that Seoul's leverage depends on maintaining its centrality in any US-led North Korea framework. The piece draws on the Lee government's concurrent security team reshuffle as the domestic political backdrop.

korea_world.headline: Saudi Arabia partners with South Korea and Ukraine for $3B air defense boost
korea_world.body_text: Saudi Arabia has entered a partnership with South Korea and Ukraine to bolster its air defenses with a combined value reported at $3 billion, as the Kingdom faces continued attacks from Iran and Houthi forces in the region.

korea_world.headline: Team Korea vows on-time completion of Czech Dukovany nuclear plant despite contractor dispute
korea_world.body_text: South Korea's nuclear project consortium reaffirmed its commitment to complete the Czech Dukovany nuclear plant on schedule despite an ongoing construction contractor dispute, pledging to 'restore trust as one team.'
